rules.title: ESM Modules
rules.check: All JavaScript files must use ES modules (import/export). CommonJS (require/module.exports) is forbidden for new code.
rules.rationale: ESM is the JavaScript standard. It enables tree shaking, static analysis, and TypeScript migration.

rules.title: TypeScript Ready
rules.check: JavaScript code must be structured for TypeScript migration. JSDoc type annotations are required.
rules.rationale: JSDoc enables TypeScript to understand JavaScript. It provides incremental typing before full migration.

rules.title: Strict Mode
rules.check: All JavaScript files must use strict mode.
rules.rationale: Strict mode catches common errors and prevents unsafe practices. It is required for modules and improves optimization.

rules.title: Const Over Let
rules.check: const must be used by default. let only for variables that are reassigned.
rules.rationale: const prevents accidental reassignment and signals intent. let should be reserved for loop counters and values that genuinely change.

rules.title: Arrow Functions
rules.check: Arrow functions must be used for callbacks and short functions. Function declarations for named functions.
rules.rationale: Arrow functions have lexical this and concise syntax. They prevent this-related bugs in callbacks.

rules.title: Template Literals
rules.check: String concatenation must use template literals for any non-trivial cases.
rules.rationale: Template literals are more readable than concatenation. They enable multiline strings and expression embedding.

rules.title: Destructuring
rules.check: Object and array destructuring must be used for extracting multiple values.
rules.rationale: Destructuring is more concise and clearer than repeated property access. It documents the values being used.

rules.title: Spread Operator
rules.check: Spread operator must be used for object copying and array manipulation.
rules.rationale: Spread is clearer than Object.assign or concat. It enables immutable update patterns.

rules.title: Optional Chaining
rules.check: Optional chaining (?.) must be used for nullable property access.
rules.rationale: Optional chaining is safer and more concise than && chains. It clearly expresses nullable intent.

rules.title: Nullish Coalescing
rules.check: Nullish coalescing (??) must be used for defaults instead of || when zero/empty string are valid.
rules.rationale: || treats falsy values as missing. ?? only treats null/undefined as missing, preserving valid empty values.

rules.title: Object Shorthand
rules.check: Use shorthand property and method syntax in object literals.
rules.rationale: Shorthand is more concise and reduces duplication. It clearly shows when property name matches variable name.

rules.title: Class Fields
rules.check: Use public class fields instead of constructor assignment for simple properties.
rules.rationale: Class fields are more declarative and concise. They clearly show class structure at the top of the definition.
